**Node Map:** A 2D MIP-map pyramid derived from the light-view map.
*   For the lowest level of the node map, iterate through all pixels of the light-view map.
*   For each subsequent level $L$ of the node map, aggregate the leaf node indices from level $L-1$.
For each pixel in level $L$, compute the lowest common ancestor of all non-empty leaf node indices from the corresponding region in level $L-1$.

**Redundancy Check:** Before computing the filtered value, the thread checks if another thread has already claimed or is computing the same target node.
*   **Empty Pixels:** If a light-view map pixel contains no photon, the corresponding leaf node index is undefined.
*   **Time Complexity:** The construction of the node map is $O(N)$ where $N$ is the number of pixels in the light-view map.
The filtering pass is $O(N)$ in the worst case (one thread per pixel), but the effective work is reduced by the termination heuristic.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires additional memory for the node map pyramid, which is $O(N)$ for the lowest level and geometrically decreasing for higher levels.
*   **Strengths:** Significantly reduces redundant computation in sparse octrees where many photons map to the same or nearby nodes.
The "upper left" heuristic may not be optimal for all thread scheduling architectures.
*   **When to Use:** When filtering sparse voxel octrees for cone tracing, especially when the light-view map has high coherence (many photons in the same node).
*   **When Not to Use:** If the octree is dense and the overhead of the node map construction outweighs the savings from thread termination.
It addresses the inefficiency of parallel MIP-map generation for sparse voxel octrees, where many threads would otherwise perform the same work due to the spatial coherence of light samples.
